title: Defined Terms: The Day a Wayfare Registration Grace Runs From
content:
These defined terms of the **Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing** product fix the day from which the registration grace runs. The registration grace days are the calendar days after a lapsed vehicle registration's expiry date on which the document hold for it begins.

### Terms

- **Registration's expiry date:** the expiry date shown on the latest vehicle registration upload on the standing record.
- **Covering expiry notice:** an expiry notice for the vehicle registration on the standing record sent for that expiry date; the first and the second notice are told apart by the notice sequence each shows.
- **Recent quality warning:** a quality warning on the standing record, of any basis, dated fewer than 3 whole calendar months before the day the grace is worked out.
- **Recent unsafe driving report:** a safety report in the unsafe driving category on the standing record dated fewer than 6 whole calendar months before that day.

### Grace-clock rule

When the standing record holds a recent quality warning and the second expiry notice covering the registration's expiry date is on record, the grace runs from that second notice's date, because a driver already under a warning was told a week ahead. When it holds no recent quality warning but holds a recent unsafe driving report and the first expiry notice covering that expiry date is on record, the grace runs from that first notice's date. Otherwise the grace runs from the registration's expiry date.

The days from the registration's expiry date to the day the grace runs from are added to the registration grace days; a notice date before the expiry date makes those days a negative number. When the grace runs from the expiry date, nothing is added.

### Truth table

| Recent quality warning | Second covering notice on record | Recent unsafe driving report | First covering notice on record | Grace runs from |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | (not read) | (not read) | the second notice's date |
| yes | no | (not read) | (not read) | the expiry date |
| no | (not read) | yes | yes | the first notice's date |
| no | (not read) | yes | no | the expiry date |
| no | (not read) | no | (not read) | the expiry date |

### Hypothetical figures

Registration expiry date 2026-04-30, first covering notice 2026-03-31, second covering notice 2026-04-23. Running from the second notice adds -7 days; running from the first notice adds -30 days; running from the expiry date adds nothing.
